articleTitle: Accurate Sub-circuit Model of LDMOS Transistor with Drift Region Emphasis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this work, we proposed a high-precision sub-circuit model on drift region to capture electrical characteristics of a lateral double-diffused MOSFET (LDMOS). The novel sub-circuit model adequately covers temperature effect, self-heating effect, impact ionization effect, and mismatch effect. The key fitting parameters have been shown of less deviation from experimental results. For example, the fitting error of vtlin (threshold voltage at linear region), idlin (on current at linear region) and idsat (on current at saturated region) are less than 6 mV, 1% and 1%, respectively. The developed SPICE model has been applied to the subsequent power circuit design, which shows good performance, further demonstrating the benefits of the model.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Power Control Strategy for Multiport Magnetic Network Energy Routers
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Magnetic network energy router (MNER) has the advantages of high transmission efficiency and high-power quality in distributed energy consumption. Traditional proportional-integral (PI) control applied to MNER converters exhibits slow dynamic response and insufficient multi-objective control capability. To solve this problem, a model predictive power control (MPPC) strategy is proposed in this paper for MNER converter, which can achieve the free flow of power between different ports, has better dynamic performance than PI control. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MPPC strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Switched-Capacitor Based Voltage Measurement for Multi-Cell Battery Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: With fast battery technology growing, multi-cell with higher energy densities requires battery management system (BMS) performs with high input voltage. Switched-capacitor architecture can be used in the high-voltage condition and combined well with the successive quantization circuits with given BCD process. However, the typical structure of switch for high-voltage sensing has some limitation to switched-capacitor measurement architecture. A modified sensing structure based on gate cross-coupled bootstrap circuit is proposed in this paper. The performance of proposed structure is simulated with 0.18um 70V BCD process at the temperature range of -40°C~125°C and process corner of TT, FF, SS, FS, SF. The simulation results show that at the high common input voltage, the measurement error is no more than 1mV.

articleTitle: A Hardware-friendly Image Mapping Parameter Matrix Compression Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Image mapping is widely applied in various fields of multi-camera video, panoramic display, medical imaging, and AR augmented reality. Generally speaking, its software implementation is a computing-intensive task and its hardware implementation needs a lot of both hardware computing resources and storage space. In order to attack such disadvantages, an efficient and hardware-friendly image mapping parameter matrix compression algorithm based on bilinear interpolation has been proposed. The proposed algorithm can theoretically achieve compression ratio with any scale and any image size, which largely benefits its circuit acceleration. The proposed algorithm has been evaluated on image quality from both subjective and objective perspectives based on both USIS-D dataset and a self-shot data, meanwhile it has been verified on a Xilinx Kintex7-325T FPGA board. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed algorithm significantly cuts down computation and storage resource consumption under the premise of losing little image quality.

articleTitle: Defect Modeling for Pre-bond TSV Considering Testing Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: To guarantee the yield of 3D-ICs, TSVs need to be tested before die bonding process. An accurate pre-bond TSV defect model is the foundation of defect testing. Conventional pre-bond TSV defect models do not consider the defect characteristics under different frequencies, which leads them not accurate enough for practical application. In this paper, we proposed pre-bond TSV RLGC equivalent lumped defect models for void, open, and pinhole defects considering testing frequency. The validity of the defect models have been proved by theoretical equations, practical measurement and Q3D simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Fault Diagnosis Mechanism based on MBIST for Embedded Memories
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper proposed a novel memory built-in self-diagnostic approach to fault localisation and fault type identification for failed memory cells. The efficiency of memory built-in self-test (MBIST) depends on the complexity of the test algorithm and its fault coverage, and the diagnosability rate of the test algorithm also determines the fault diagnosis capability. Therefore, it is necessary to analyse the test and diagnostic capability of the test algorithm to determine its diagnosability rate. In order to avoid the tedium of manual analysis, this paper describes an automated analysis procedure that enables the performance analysis of memory test algorithms. When a memory cell fails, it is necessary to diagnose the error and analyse its error address, data, current algorithm operation steps and other information in order to locate the error and make a quick and correct remedy for subsequent repair. Therefore, a fault diagnosis mechanism is proposed that realises the identification of fault types by capturing the march syndrome recognised during MBIST execution.

articleTitle: An LMS-based Calibration Technique Using On-chip PN Signal for SAR ADCs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper introduces a calibration technique for capacitor mismatches in a Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC, based on the Least Mean Square (LMS) algorithm. The Capacitor Digital-to-analog Converter (CDAC) in a SAR ADC is reused and driven by a Pseudo-Random (PN) sequence generator, generating on-chip analog input signals for LMS calibration. A dynamic iteration step size is implemented to increase convergence speed and accuracy. The calibration circuit does not sacrifice the conversion speed or significantly increase the hardware as traditional LMS-based calibration techniques. The calibration technique is verified based on a 14-bit SAR ADC model. Compared with the results before calibration, this work improve the Spurious Free Dynamic Range (SFDR) performance from 63.4dbc to 106.5dbc. Additionally, the Integral Nonlinearity (INL) performance improved from 50LSBs to 2LSBs.

articleTitle: A Frequency-to-Voltage Converter-Based Frequency-Locked Loop for Injection Locking PLL
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Injection locking technique can effectively increase loop bandwidth of Phase Locked Loop (PLL)without introducing stability issues. However, the capture range of injection locking PLL (ILPLL) are limited to 1/2 • Fref due to its inherent phase alignment method, which need an additional power hungry frequency tracking loop (FLL) to address the issue. This paper presents that a frequency-voltage converter based FLL makes it possible for ILPLLs to lock with any initial frequency. To extract the frequency information of the output signal, a low power capacitor-charged FVC is design instead of traditional charge pump. Combined the pulse swallower counter, the proposed ILPLL can be locked over the entire tuning range of the oscillator. The circuit is designed on a 40nm CMOS process. The simulation results shows that the proposed FLL consumes 5.7mW and its locking time less than 1us which is more power efficiency compared to the previous FLLs. The simulated reference spur and phase noise were -45 dBc and -124.3 dBc/Hz at 1MHz with 2.2-GHz output frequency.

articleTitle: A Digital System for High-Speed Measurement of Capacitance under Transient Stress Impact
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) are often used in transient high stress impact scenarios, with a stress impact pulse width of sub milliseconds. In order to study the dynamic characteristics of MLCCs under impact stress, it is necessary to obtain the capacitance and its variation of MLCCs during the stress action time. This paper designs a digital system for high-speed capacitance measurement, which can obtain the transient voltage of MLCC and store it in non-volatile memory. A prototype was designed with a data conversion period of 160ns. The functionality of the prototype was verified through Hopkinson pressure bar impact experiment. The transient capacitance of MLCC was calculated based on the transient voltage value, achieving high-speed and accurate measurement of capacitance.

articleTitle: GNN-Curio: Transistor Sizing by Curiosity-Driven Reinforcement Learning with Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In recent years, several methods using deep reinforcement learning (DRL) have been published in the field of analog circuit sizing, and all these methods have outperformed previous methods and even human design. However, these are limited to basic circuits with a minimal number of elements and desired specifications, and may not be effective for the large-scale topologies and specifications required in actual design situations. We introduce the Graph Neural Network (GNN)-Curio method, which combines effective feature extraction via GNN with an internal reward scheme named "curiosity" to enable exploration in large-scale topologies and specifications. The GNN-Curio has demonstrated the ability to achieve a Figure of Merit (FoM) with more than tenfold precision for topologies with over 25 elements, which is unattainable by existing DRL methods.

articleTitle: Exact lock-in range for a second-order PLL with discontinuous sawtooth phase detector characteristic
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In the present work, we show how the development of the theory of differential equations with discontinuous right-hand sides allows to analyze a modern electronic system used for synchronization of signals. An exact solution to the Gardner problem on the lock-in range is obtained for a second-order type 2 phase-locked loop (PLL) with a sawtooth phase detector characteristic for the first time.

articleTitle: True-Single-Phase-Clock Dual-Edge-Triggering Flip-Flop Based on Low Power Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper proposes a method of low power True-Single-Phase-Clock(TSPC) dual-edge-triggering flip-flop based on low power control technology. The method analyzes the working states of the internal nodes of TSPC structure, combines the low power control technology and the necessary jump conditions of each node, eliminates the redundant switching activity of internal nodes, improves the circuit structure, and has no current competition’s phenomenon. The power consumption and total power delay product are reduced. Compared with the single-transistor clocked dual edge triggering flip-flop(STC-DET) which has the lowest power consumption measured, the simulation results show that the power consumption of the circuit with 28nm technology at 1.2V and 0.6V is reduced by 9.7% and 6.1%. At the same time, the experimental results show: the power consumption and delay of the designed circuit are better than other literatures.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Dual Ramp Generator for Two-Step Single-Slope ADCs in CMOS Image Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a novel hybrid dual ramp generator for a two-step single-slope analog-to-digital converter (TS SS ADC). In this circuit, an R-2R DAC has been designed to replace the R-string DAC in the traditional coarse ramp generator, as a result the resolution can be improved in the coarse ramp stage and the conversion time of hybrid dual ramp generator can be decreased. The proposed hybrid dual ramp generator with coarse resolution of 5bit and fine resolution of 6bit has been designed and implemented in a 110nm CMOS process. The simulation results show that it can generate an output ramp voltage range of 0-2V, with a conversion time of 2 μs at the clock frequency of 50 MHz.

articleTitle: Design of Integrated Voltage and Current Bandgap Reference with Low Temperature Drift
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: It is difficult to design chips with both bandgap voltage source and bandgap current source because of resistors with temperature coefficient, which leads to separate bandgap circuits, bigger die size and higher cost. This paper proposes a bandgap circuit with the integration of voltage and current reference. Based on the study of the traditional reference current source and voltage source, this paper presents the reference power supply circuit module configured with resistors, which includes the PTAT current circuit with the operational amplifier for the reference voltage, the CTAT current circuit and the current mirror for the reference current. The simultaneous output of bandgap reference voltage and bandgap reference current is based on the coupling of the PTAT and the CTAT circuit with the reference voltage loop and the reference current loop, sharing several components of the PTAT circuit and operational amplifier circuit. The simulation and evaluation results show that the bandgap reference circuit proposed in this paper is able to provide stable outputs over a wide temperature range, and both the voltage and current outputs demonstrate better temperature stability.

articleTitle: A 0.638 ppm/°C Precision Bandgap Reference With Multi-Segment Current Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The paper presented a high-accuracy bandgap reference (BGR) with multi-segment linear current compensation, achieving a low temperature coefficient (TC) over a wide temperature range. By segmenting the output voltage of the traditional first-order BGR and applying temperature compensation in each segment, the output voltage across all temperature ranges is stabilized to a consistent level, effectively reducing TC. The proposed bandgap reference is designed based on a 180nm CMOS process and achieves an average output voltage of 0.93 V; The best TC is 0.638 ppm/°C with a wide temperature range of -40°C to 150°C. The circuit consumes 17 μA at a supply voltage of 1.8 V. Additionally, it exhibits a line regulation (LR) of 0.023%/V across a supply voltage range from 1.5 V to 2.5 V.

articleTitle: A 13-b 20-MS/s SAR ADC with Capacitor mismatch Calibration combining ADC Self-Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a 13-b, 20-MS/s successive-approximation-register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). A capacitance mismatch calibration method based on the time domain comparator and time-to-digital convert (TDC) combining SAR ADC self-calibration is proposed to achieve high precision. The calibration circuit looks simple enough, and the calibration process costs just 23us. A capacitor with a capacity of only 1fF is designed to be used as a unit capacitor to improve the speed and accuracy of voltage setting. The simulation result shows that the signal-to-noise distortion ratio (SNDR) of ADC is up to 80.62dB, and the spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) is 95.9dB at a supply voltage of 1.2V and a sampling rate of 20 MS/s.

articleTitle: A Low-temperature Compensated High-precision Bandgap Reference
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The paper presents a novel bandgap reference voltage source structure that offers several advantages, including low-temperature coefficient, high supply voltage rejection ratio (PSRR), and low current consumption. The bandgap reference voltage source is designed using a 180 nm CMOS process and implemented in a circuit with a core area of 400 μm × 120 μm (excluding PAD). Simulated results demonstrate that the bandgap reference has an stable output voltage of 0.559 V, a minimum output temperature coefficient of 0.474 ppm/℃ over the temperature range of -40 ℃ to 125 ℃, and an optimal PSRR of - 92.566 dB@100Hz, with a supply voltage of 1.8 V. The bandgap reference's current consumption is only 21.67 μA under typical conditions, and simulation test results indicate that the bandgap reference exhibits low-temperature coefficient and high PSRR, making it suitable for high-precision signal chain applications.

articleTitle: A 60-GHz Distributed CTLE with Complementary Units for 240-Gb/s Receiver in 28-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a distributed CTLE with complementary unit as the analog front end of 240-Gb/s wireline receivers. By distributing more CTLE units among the artificial transmission lines, the DC gain of the CTLE can be increased without reducing bandwidth or degrading impedance matching. Compared to lumped CTLEs which realize a high peak gain by cascading multiple stages, the single-stage distributed CTLE achieves higher peak frequency and linearity. To enhance power efficiency, the CTLE unit is implemented with a complementary structure and common-mode feedback, which allows zero voltage drop on the termination resistors. Implemented in a 28-nm CMOS process, the proposed CTLE achieves an 11.1 dB peak gain at 60 GHz with only 60 mW power consumption. It can compensate for a 10.1 dB channel loss with an output amplitude larger than the input.

articleTitle: Enhancing Local Wireless Communication Capacity in Distribution Substation Areas—A Systematic Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: With the development of smart grid, the number of end terminals and data collection frequency are gradually increasing and the interaction characteristics are becoming more and more obvious. Therefore, local wireless communication network in the distribution substation areas faces many challenges in terms of capacity, coverage, security, reliability, and etc. It is necessary to research new wireless communication technologies and network structures to meet the growing demands for high frequency data collection and interaction in the distribution substation areas. This paper firstly analyzes the business characteristics of local wireless communication in the distribution substation areas and the unique features of the 230MHz band dedicated for electric power systems. Then, a systematic perspective for enhancing local wireless communication capacity by applying carrier aggregation in the 230MHz frequency band is given. In particular, a physical layer data aggregation scheme is designed and a structure for multi-user parallel carrier aggregation based on multi-phase filter banks is proposed. This work can provide guidance for the design of wireless communication system and network in the distribution substation areas.

articleTitle: 112-Gb/s PAM-4 Transmitter With Differential Encoding and XOR Driver in 28-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This article presents a 112-Gb/s pulse amplitude modulation 4-level (PAM-4) transmitter (TX) with differential encoding and XOR (exclusive OR) driver in 28-nm CMOS technology. Compared to the TXs using a 4:1 multiplexer (MUX) based on four-way interleaved 1-UI pulse generators, this design utilizes an XOR driver for serialization, which reduces the loading of the four-phase 14-GHz clock and eliminates the use of 1-UI pulse generator circuit to save power consumption. The main innovations of this work include the differential encoder RZ (return-to-zero) retimer, and XOR tailless driver. The simulation results indicate that the energy efficiency for the PAM-4 TX is 1.13pJ/b at 112 Gb/s with a 1-Vppd output amplitude.

articleTitle: A Low Transient Overshoot Voltage Single Inductor Bipolar Output for AMOLED Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive constant on-time control mode for the single inductor bipolar output (SIBO) converter for active-matrix organic light-emitting diode (AMOLED) displays to improve the load transient response. The proposed SIBO converter generates bipolar output with only a two-phase operation without additional phase adjustment. The adaptive current structure (ACC) eliminates the mismatch between positive and negative outputs and ensures the converter to operate stably under the control of ACOT. The proposed converter is implemented using HHGBCD 0.18µm CMOS process. The simulation results show that SIBO can provide stable 4.6V positive output and -6V negative output at 1.25MHz operating frequency, and the maximum output current is 300mA. In the ACOT control mode, when the output current varies between 50mA and 300mA, the overshoot voltage is 42mV and the undershoot voltage is 48mV, which effectively reduces the transient overshoot voltage of SIBO.

IEEE Keywords: Active matrix organic light emitting diodes

articleTitle: A 13.4-31.8-GHz Single-core Dual-mode VCO with Mode-independent Transformer-switching Technique in 55nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a single-core dual-mode millimeter-wave (mm-wave) voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) using a compact dual-mode LC network with a mode-independent switched transformer technique is proposed with SMIC 55-nm CMOS design kit. Each core contains a 4-bit switched capacitor array and a switchable transformer to maximize the entire tuning range. In simulation results, the proposed oscillator exhibits a 81.4% tunning range from 13.4 to 31.8 GHz. The best phase noise at 1-MHz offset is -115.4 dBc/Hz, corresponding to the frequency of 13.4 GHz. The VCO consumes 8.38-to-14.88 mW from a 0.6 V supply voltage, achieving 192.32 dBc/Hz FOM and 212.32 dBc/Hz FOMT, respectively. The core area is 0.066 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Scalable Model for GaN HEMTs with Trapping and Self-Heating Effects Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: A scaling rule suitable for GaN HEMTs with different gate widths is proposed to address the problem of repeated parameter extraction and cumbersome modeling. Firstly, an initial nonlinear model was established as the scaling benchmark. Second, targeting the scaling rules for parasitic capacitance, inductance, and gate/drain finger inductance establish scaling rules to characterize large signal models. Finally, the validation results of GaN HEMTs devices with different gate widths and number of gate fingers show that the scaling model proposed in this paper can accurately simulate the S-parameter and DC I-V.

articleTitle: A 60-68GHz Three-coil-Coupling VCO Achieving 186dBc/Hz FoM in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a quad-core LC VCO design was implemented using 28nm CMOS technology. The tuning range achieved was 60 GHz to 68 GHz (12.5%). In this design, the four identical VCO cores were synchronized using mode suppression, and the use of slab inductor allowed for breaking the frequency limitations. Each VCO core employed three coupling coils to increase V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf> . At 60 GHz, a phase noise performance of -104.8 dBc/Hz was achieved at 1 MHz frequency offset. The VCO consumed 24 mW power, and the figure of merit (FoM) at 1 MHz offset was 186 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: Design of a Low-power, High SNR Rolling Shutter 64-stage TDI Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The paper proposes a high-speed, high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) 64-stage time delay integration (TDI) image sensor. To improve the line rate of the sensor, we partition the pixel array along the horizontal direction and read pixel information from both sides towards the middle. Additionally, we introduce a bypass current in the readout circuit to speed up clamp circuit establishment. Moreover, this sensor achieves better SNR performance due to noiseless charge transfer in the charge domain and noise robustness of the open-loop comparator. The proposed technique is experimentally verified on a 512 × 128 pixel TDI image sensor fabricated using a 55 nm CMOS process. Test results demonstrate that at a line rate of 3980 lines/s, the SNR can reach 67 dB at 64 stage. Compared with other work, there is an increase of 2.7% in line rate and 16.7% in SNR while maintaining low power consumption.

articleTitle: A 10-15 GHz CMOS Balun-LNA Using Folded Three-Coil Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a 10-15 GHz low noise amplifier (LNA) in 40nm CMOS technology. It consists of cascode stage and common source (CS) stage. The transformer between cascode stage and CS stage is applied as a passive balun to achieve single-to-differential conversion. By utilizing a folded three-coil transformer in input matching network, compact layout and wideband input matching are achieved. In addition, the coupled coils boost the equivalent transconductance of input transistor and realize noise reduction simultaneously. The simulated results show outstanding performance. S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> is lower than -10 dB from 7.2 GHz to 18.8 GHz. Within the operating frequency range of 10-15 GHz, the noise figure (NF) is below 2.15 dB and the minimum NF is 2.02 dB. The average gain is 22.1 dB and the gain flatness is ±1.1 dB. The power consumption is 23.3 mW.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband High Spurious Suppression Frequency Synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Frequency synthesizer plays an important part in RF systems, which generates different kinds of RF signals required by the system, including the transmit signal, the local oscillator signal and the reference signal. This paper presents a design of a broadband high spurious suppression frequency synthesizer. The design uses direct digital synthesis (DDS) baseband combined with phase-locked dielectric resonance oscillator (PDRO) and phase-locked loop (PLL) point frequency for frequency conversion, and realizes high spurious suppression by selecting suitable frequency combination. The testing results of the frequency synthesizer are as follows: Output frequency: 12-20GHz, output power ⩾10dBm, spurious suppression ⩾ 70dBc, phase noise ⩽-104dBc/Hz@1kHz. The synthesizer has the advantages of small size, wide operating band, high spurious suppression and low phase noise.

articleTitle: A Novel Seamless PFM/PWM Mode Switching Circuit in Peak Current Mode Controlled Buck Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a seamless transition circuit for PWM/PFM in a peak-current-mode-controlled buck converter. By adding clamp circuitry and a circuit module for frequency reduction based on clamp current to the existing PWM loop control, PFM is achieved without the need for an additional control circuit ,which reduces circuit complexity while enhancs detection and control accuracy. The frequency reduction generated by the PFM controller automatically adjusts according to changes in feedback voltage, thereby improving the system's dynamic response characteristics. Additionally, during operation in PFM mode, the PWM control module is deactivated, reducing system losses. The proposed seamless transition circuit is applied to a peak-current-mode-controlled buck converter and simulated in 0.18um CMOS process. The simulation results indicate that the system achieves a smooth transition between PWM and PFM modes. During the switching process, the transient variation in output voltage is less than 42mV, demonstrating favorable dynamic response characteristics. The buck converter using the seamless PWM/PFM transition control achieves 97.1% peak efficiency.

articleTitle: An Improved High-Reliability Level Shifter for Gallium Nitride Transistor Half-Bridge Based on Current Mirror Differential Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Gallium Nitride transistors are increasingly becoming the preferred choice for power electronic converters due to their superior switching characteristics. Their gate drivers require level shifters with high noise immunity and low latency to ensure stable operation during high-frequency switching. This paper presents an improved level shifter based on a current mirror cross coupled structure, which translates a voltage domain of 0V-5V to a 35V-40V range. The proposed design enhances the traditional structure by adding an error current preprocessing stage to achieve higher power slew-rate immunity. The circuit is fabricated using a 0.35um HVCMOS process and validated with a 1MHz square wave signal. The result shows that the circuit's slew-rate immunity exceeds 700V/ns, with a rise delay of 1.462ns and a fall delay of 1.406ns.

articleTitle: A Neurostimulator with Differential Charge Packet Injection Charge Balancing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: A neurostimulator system is presented in this paper to provide a configurable current stimulus patterns for Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS). The stimulation system utilizes eight standard H-bridge current stimulators, each capable of generating a stimulation current of up to ±2.55mA. A novel charge recovery circuit of differential charge packet injection (DCPI) is proposed to achieve high-precision charge recovery. The neurostimulator is implemented in a 0.18μm BCD process. DCPI technique is used to reduce the residual voltage on the electrode-electrolyte interface during the inter-pulse time interval, which achieve 3 mV charge balancing precision with less sequential logic.

articleTitle: A Low Phase Noise and Ultra-Wideband Voltage-Controlled Oscillator Based on 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to realize a low phase noise ultra-wideband Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) using 65nm CMOS technology. The core circuit of the oscillator employs PMOS cross-coupled pairs to generate second harmonic signals, constituting the push-push structure. Transformer coupling technique is utilized for single-ended to differential signal conversion, and a 3-bit switched capacitor array is designed for wide-range frequency modulation, thereby broadening the operational frequency band of the oscillator. The fundamental oscillation frequency of the proposed VCO is from 3GHz to 5GHz, thus generates a frequency tuning range of 5.7GHz to 10.2GHz for the second harmonic signal. The measured phase noise at a 1MHz offset from the center frequency at room temperature (25°C) is -122.4dBc/Hz. Under a 2.5V power supply, the VCO’s overall power consumption typically ranges around 12.35mW.

articleTitle: A 91.1% Peak Efficiency Multi-Input Energy Harvesting Interface With High Accurate Hybrid MPPT
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper proposed a multi-input high-efficiency energy harvesting interface which is simultaneously harvesting from thermoelectric (TEG), photovoltaic (PV), and piezoelectric (PZT) energy sources. The design utilizes a hybrid MPPT design and an adaptive switching cycle (ASC) scheme to track the maximum power point (MPPT) of the sources to achieve higher MPPT accuracy and end-to-end efficiency, and converting the piezoelectric energy rectified by a parallel synchronized switch harvesting on inductive (P-SSHI) rectifier and the thermoelectric and photoelectric energy into adjustable output. The interface is designed by HGBD 0.18μm CMOS process and simulated at the system level by using the Cadence Spectre tool, the results show that the maximum output power of the circuit is 15mW, and peak MPPT efficiencies of the thermoelectric, photovoltaic, and piezoelectric are 99.73%, 99.87%, and 99.22%, the peak end-to-end efficiency of the circuit is 91.1%.

articleTitle: A True Random Number Generator Based on Spin Torque Nano-Oscillator and Phase Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: True random numbers, derived from unpredictable physical processes, are essential for ensuring the security of information systems through cryptographic applications such as secure encryption key generation and authentication mechanisms. In this study, we introduce a novel True Random Number Generator (TRNG) architecture leveraging a Spin Torque Nano-Oscillator (STNO) integrated with a meticulously designed phase-locked loop (PLL). The oscillation frequency fluctuations of the STNO, induced by thermal noise, serve as the primary source of entropy. To maximize synchronization, an auxiliary PLL loop is employed to align the rising edges of the sampling signal with those of the entropy source signal. Despite the inherent phase noise of the STNO, the PLL maintains a metastable state between locking and losing lock, further enhancing the randomness and unpredictability of the generated bitstream. Finally, we evaluate and discuss the performance of the proposed TRNG circuit.

articleTitle: A Sense Amplifier Using Resistive Feedback for Offset Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: As the size of the dynamic random access memory (DRAM) shrinks, offset voltage caused by transistor mismatch seriously affects the performance of data reading. In this paper, a sense amplifier with resistive feedback (RFSA) and a sense amplifier with common resistive feedback (CRFSA) are proposed to compensate the offset of bit-line sense amplifier (BLSA) in DRAM. In this way, the initial node voltage of the sense amplifier could be set very close to the metastable-point. Simulation results show that the offset voltage is reduced by more than 90% (RFSA) and 70% (CRFSA) compared with the offset mismatch calibration sense amplifier (OMCSA). In addition, under circumstances of different transistor sizes, large bit-line capacitance, temperature changes, etc., RFSA and CRFSA both have excellent performance in offset compensation, thus having a significant advantage in eliminating the effects of process fluctuations on the BLSA offset.

articleTitle: A 2-18 GHz, 6-bit True Time Delay Chain with 378 ps Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a highly integrated 6-bit 2-18 GHz true time delay (TTD) circuit for multi-band phased array systems covering S-band to Ku-band based on 130 nm SOI technology. 3D electromagnetic simulation is optimized for the artificial transmission line (ATL) and all-pass network (APN) units in the delay chain to achieve a smaller on-chip area footprint. The TTD designed in this paper has a maximum delay of up to 378 ps, a minimum step of 6 ps, a root-mean-square (RMS) error of less than 8.14 ps, and a maximum insertion loss of less than 18 dB. The entire ultra-wideband delay circuit and the related functional modules are described in this paper, which has been verified by post-simulation and is now in the process of tape out.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Approximate Softmax Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Deep learning is rapidly advancing. However, the increasing computational demands present challenges for high- efficient hardware implementations. A novel softmax architecture based on approximate computing is proposed. The exponential operation in softmax is transformed from base e to base 2. Additionally, Goldschmidt approximate algorithm is applied to simplify division operation. Through segmented approximate radix-4 Booth multipliers, the area and power consumption are effectively reduced while maintaining high accuracy. The proposed design is synthesized under SMIC 28-nm CMOS technology and tested on Vision Transformer classifying the ImageNet dataset. Compared with the state of the art, proposed approximate softmax achieves up to 64.1 times area efficiency while maintaining high precision.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Silicon-Based Active Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband active phase shifter covering S, C, X, and Ku bands. The proposed phase shifter consists of the ultra-wideband balun, I/Q signal generation module, vector modulation and control module, and compensation amplifier. The ultra-wideband balun uses an improved Marchand balun structure to ensure low amplitude and phase error across the frequency range of 2-18GHz. The I/Q quadrature signal generation module utilizes the polyphase filter (PPF) to extend bandwidth and enhance the signal accuracy. Besides, the vector modulation and control module achieve high-precision vector modulation functions through switch-controlled Gilbert cells and current mirrors. The function of the compensation amplifier is to optimize the gain flatness of this phase shifter. Simulation results show that the ultra-wideband phase shifter exhibits an insertion loss of less than 8dB and the RMS phase error is less than 2.28° over 2-18GHz. The chip area is 1.15mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The power consumption of the phase shifter is 36.35mW from a 1V voltage supply and the core circuit power consumption is 3.84mW.

articleTitle: A 64Gb/s PAM4 Transmitter Achieving a Reconfigurable Output Swing Range from 0.333V to 1V without Stress Issue
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents a quarter-rate transmitter (TX) supporting 32Gb/s non-return-to-zero (NRZ) and 64Gb/s four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4). The TX incorporates a novel bias circuit structure to address the voltage stress issue when the reconfigurable differential peak-to-peak swing (VPPD) ranges from 0.333V to 1V. The key circuits include a quarter-rate pre-driver and a 7-bit digital-to-analog converter (DAC) based current-mode logic (CML) driver. The simulation results indicate that the TX operates without stress issues in both NRZ and PAM4 modes at various output swing configurations. The TX exhibits random jitter (RJ) is 131 fsrms with a 1VPPD swing and 132 fsrms with 0.333 VPPD swing, and achieves an energy efficiency of 1.35 pJ/bit at 64Gb/s PAM4 with a 1VPPD swing.

articleTitle: A Wideband 6-bit Phase Shifter with Low Insertion Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Based on the 0.25-μm GaAs pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (pHEMT) process, a 6-18 GHz low insertion loss 6-bit phase shifter chip with digital driver was developed. In order to achieve low insertion loss, wide-bandwidth, and high phase-shifting accuracy, different structures are used: 5.625°, 11.25°, and 22.5° phase-shifting bits with a bridge T-type structure; 45° and 90° phase-shifting bits with a switched high-low pass filter structure; and 180° phase-shifting with a Lange coupler. The driver unit employs a direct-coupled field-effect transistor logic (DCFL) structure. Simulation results show that the insertion loss of the phase shifter is less than 9 dB, the root-mean-square error (RMS) of the phase shifter is less than 8°, the amplitude variation is ±1 dB, and the input-output return loss is less than -10 dB in the operating frequency band of 6-18 GHz. The chip size is 2.9 mm × 1.87 mm, and it is characterized by wideband and low insertion loss.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Multiplexing Drive Circuit for Spaceborne Stepper Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Stepper motor is widely used in various space optical load mechanism, the number of traditional drive circuits and motors is consistent. This paper designs the multiplexing drive circuit for spaceborne stepper motor, which can effectively reduce the volume, weight and cost of the circuit. In order to ensure the long-term reliable operation of the circuit, the selection of diode parameters in the multiplexing drive circuit is crucial. In view of the situation that the oscilloscope can not directly measure the transient high voltage, it is necessary to invert the voltage value with current. The simulation model of stepper motor multiplexing drive circuit is established based on simulation software, and the influence of oscilloscope probe on diode voltage test is analyzed. The simulation results show that for the controlled load stepper motor, the voltage value of the diode measured is reduced by nearly 24V compared with the actual value due to the influence of oscilloscope probe. For the actual circuit, it is necessary to consider the reasonable configuration of diodes to prevent the circuit damage caused by reverse overvoltage.

articleTitle: A Solar Powered General Purpose IoT Node for Smart Grid Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: At present, the application of Internet of Things technology in the power industry has been applied in multiple fields such as equipment monitoring and management, intelligent meter reading and energy management, etc. In order to adapt to the diverse applications in the power industry, IoT nodes need to provide sufficient universality to connect different devices and sensors and sufficient power supply capacity. In this paper, a solar powered general purpose IoT node for smart grid applications is presented. By considering various potential connection methods, the presented IoT node provides sufficient peripheral interfaces to adapt to different devices and sensors. In sunny conditions, the presented IoT node can effectively collect solar energy for power supply. Meanwhile, its communication capability has good isotropic consistency.

articleTitle: Research on Weight Update Modulation of Memflash for Adaptive Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Different from traditional binary iterative weight update methods, neuromorphic chip, in favor of analog computation based on physical laws, has significantly enhanced computational efficiency. As a typical component of neuromorphic chip, memristor faces the limitation of resistance fluctuation, stability and adjustment range in weight updating control. To overcome these defects, this study proposes an innovative design of a common-gate non-conjugated memflash. Utilizing advanced transfer layer stacking technology, the dynamic range of weight updates has been significantly expanded from 1.87×10⁻⁹A to 4.41×10⁻⁷A, providing a broader adjustment space for neuromorphic computing. Additionally, through customized molecular interface modification technology, the accuracy of weight updates has been improved and a weight update relaxation model has been established, achieving precise and controllable weight adjustment. At the device array level, by adopting a strategy of common-source and common-gate grounding with independent drain control, the crosstalk between devices has been effectively eliminated. This provides a stable foundation for the array to perform matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) operations. The common-gate non-conjugated memflash proposed in this study has not only optimized the weight update mechanism but also enhanced the computational control capabilities of hardware adaptive circuits.

articleTitle: A High-Input Impedance Chopper Capacitively Coupled Instrumentation Amplifier With DC Offset Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: An improved chopper capacitively coupled instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) is proposed for electrocardiogram (ECG) signal acquisition applications. Impedance boosting techniques improve the input impedance. The direct current servo loop (DSL) along with a programmable DC offset compensation module suppresses electrode offset. The CCIA, fabricated in 0.18μm CMOS, achieves an input impedance of 2.2GΩ and suppresses electrode offset up to 230mV under 1.8V supply. The input-referred noise of 1.4 μVrms is measured with 2.07 μW power consumption.

articleTitle: A Low Power Capacitive Sensor Readout Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: To quantify the capacitance of a capacitive sensor, this paper adopts the same supply voltage (VDD) stable charging current and comparison threshold for both the local and external sensor relaxation oscillators, enabling the local counter to quantize the frequency of the sensor relaxation oscillator with minimal circuit complexity and power consumption. Additionally, when the sensor is utilized as a capacitive switch, since the capacitance variation trend between the on-chip capacitor and the external sensor is inconsistent, make the sensor state inaccurate. Therefore, this paper also presents a detection mechanism based on a comparison between the count values of sensor oscillator in preceding and subsequent time windows. An auxiliary instantaneous reference is also used to determine whether the sensor returns to its previous state. This mechanism enables the high precision and broad range detection of changes in the sensor’s capacitance, effectively mitigating erroneous state transitions. Test results show that the maximum current consumed by the entire readout circuit is less than 2 μA, and it can detect the capacitance variation of 1% when the capacitance of sensor is in the range of 10~20 pF.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Asynchronous SAR ADC Employing Metastability Detection and Hardware Reused Skip Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: A single-channel high-speed asynchronous successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is presented in this paper. Considering that the metastability error occurs when the input signal is approximately equal to zero, a novel metastability error detection technique is presented. Moreover, based on this, a hardware reused skip technique is proposed to relax the timing design requirement in SAR logic loops. These techniques enable a 500 MS/s 9-bit asynchronous SAR ADC in a 22-nm CMOS process. Simulation results show that the proposed techniques help to reduce the metastability error, increase the conversion speed, and improve the power efficiency of the SAR ADC.

articleTitle: A 6-9GHz DTC-based Fractional-N Sub-sampling PLL
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a digital-to-time converter (DTC)-based fractional-N sub-sampling phase locked loop (PLL) based on 28nm CMOS technology is presented. The PLL achieved an output frequency range of 6GHz to 9GHz with a power consumption of 37mW. Specifically, at an output frequency of 7.975GHz, the fractional spur with a 30% DTC gain error is - 58.75dB. After gain calibration and threshold mismatch calibration, the fractional spur is reduced by 11dB to -69.8dB. Furthermore, the phase noise is -116dBc/Hz@1MHz, and the rms jitter is 113fs.

articleTitle: A 13-bit low-power SAR ADC with a modified bottom-plate switching strategy based on split capacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a 13-bit high-precision low-power SAR ADC is proposed. Compared with the conventional common-mode voltage-based switching strategy, the proposed improved split-capacitor switching strategy effectively saves the design of the common-mode voltage reference circuit and the drive circuit, thus reducing the power consumption. In order to ensure the sampling accuracy, the switching strategy is changed from the conventional top plate switching strategy to the bottom plate switching strategy, which reduces the charge injection effect associated with the input. Based on TSMC 65nm CMOS process, a 13-bit 20MS/s SAR ADC is designed to validate the proposed technique, and the schematic design and layout design are completed with a layout area of 124.69um*159.31um.The post-simulation results show that, under the conditions of supply voltage and reference voltage of 1.2V and sampling frequency of 20MHz, the signal-to-noise distortion ratio (SNDR) reaches 80.618dB, the spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) reaches 95.798dB, and the power consumption of the analog circuit part is 196uW.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a 4th-order Feedforward Compensated Operational Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis and design of a 4th-order feedforward compensated operational amplifier for applications in continuous-time bandpass delta-sigma modulators. A new design method is proposed and analysed on the system level. Based on the proposed method, a 4th-order feedforward compensated operational amplifier is designed in a 65 nm CMOS process. With 400 fF capacitance load, the op amp consumes 10.8 mA from a supply voltage of 1.2 V. It is conditionally stable with a phase margin of 72.1 degrees and has gains of 64.6 dB, 40.0 dB and 11.5 dB at DC, 340 MHz and 1 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: A 5.5-to-8.2GHz Class-F23 Quad-Core-Oscillator Achieving 191.1dBc/Hz FoM in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this paper, a three-winding transformer-based Class-F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</inf> Quad-Core VCO is proposed. By using a three-winding transformer, the common-mode (CM) resonances around the second harmonic and the differential-mode (DM) resonances around the third harmonic are extended while maintaining the operation of Class- F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">23</inf> VCO. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, the continuous tuning range of the proposed VCO is 39.4%, from 5.5 to 8.2 GHz. The minimum phase noise is −135.1 dBc/Hz at the 1MHz offset of 5.5GHz, corresponding to the VCO figure of merit (FoM) of 191.1 dBc/Hz. The 1/f<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> phase noise corner is 180 to 230 kHz over the tuning range.

articleTitle: A DC-18 GHz 6-Bit GaAs Attenuator With High Attenuation Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In response to the demand for ultra-wideband digitally controlled attenuators in the field of microwave communication, this study fabricated a digital-driven 6-bit attenuator chip operating in the DC~18 GHz range using 0.15 μm GaAs pHEMT technology. The attenuator consists of six cascaded basic attenuation units, each employing appropriate circuit topology to achieve objectives such as low insertion loss, high attenuation accuracy, low additional phase shift, and miniaturization. Additionally, our study introduced a phase compensation structure on the traditional attenuator topology to further reduce the additional phase shift of the attenuator. Simulation results of the chip demonstrate a dynamic attenuation range from 0.5 dB to 31.5 dB, with insertion loss less than 4.3 dB, input and output return loss exceeding -12 dB, root mean square attenuation accuracy (64 states) less than 0.3 dB, and additional phase shift of all attenuation states less than 6°. Furthermore, the dimensions of the chip are 2.6 mm × 0.9 mm × 0.1 mm.

articleTitle: A 14-bit Pipelined-SAR ADC With Offset and Bit-Weight Calibration Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: This work presents a 14-bit 100 MS/s Pipelined Successive-Approximation-Register (SAR) ADC in a 28nm CMOS process. The proposed calibration technique remedies the offset voltage and bit-weight deviations that include capacitor mismatches and inter-stage gain error. The comparator offset calibration scheme employs a shift-bit logic together with an R-2R digital-to-analog converter (DAC). An improved SAR logic circuit is also proposed to generate asynchronous timing and store the results. The capacitor mismatches are calibrated in a foreground way while the inter-stage gain error is corrected in a background way using least mean square (LMS) algorithm. With the above calibration and circuit techniques, the spurious-free-dynamic-range (SFDR) is improved to 90.64dBc, while the effective-number-of-bits(ENOB) is 11.89-bit. The 14-bit 100 MS/s ADC is simulated in a 28nm CMOS process and the figure of merit (FOM) value achieves 10.86 fJ/conversion-step.

articleTitle: A Regulated Charge Pump-Based Pulse Driver Achieving Fast Dual-Edge Transition
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: High-voltage(HV) pulse drivers are widely required in MEMS actuators. This paper presents a fully integrated charge-pump(CP)–based HV pulse driver using pulse-frequency modulation (PFM) to accelerate dual-edge transition. A chopper, synchronized with the pulse control signal, is utilized to establish closed-loop regulation during both the charging and discharging phases. Unlike other published designs, this work effectively reduces both rise and fall times without compromising the CP’s drive capability. This work is designed in a standard 65nm bulk CMOS process. This driver can generate >10 V pulse output from a 2.5 V supply for a 15 pF // 50 kΩ load at 100 kHz, achieving a rise time of 407 ns and a fall time of 966 ns. It reduces 58% in rise time and 16% in fall time, respectively. While there is a trade-off between speed and power efficiency, the efficiency penalty diminishes with lower driving frequencies, ultimately improved efficiency can be achieved due to low-frequency operation during the discharging phase.

articleTitle: A Hardware Unit for Single-Precision Floating-Point Inverse Square Root with Harmonized Parabolic Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: In this work, we propose a novel method based on Harmonized Parabolic Synthesis, which combines parabolic synthesis and second-degree interpolation, to implement inverse square root hardware for IEEE single-precision floating-point format on FPGA. The implementations meet the precision requirement of 1 ULP.The experimental results show that the proposed implementation demonstrates either lower resource usage, shorter execution latency, higher clock rate, or higher throughput when compared to other works (including Intel IP), which use various methods such as polynomial approximation and enhanced Quake algorithm.The presented floating-point inverse square root unit is suitable for high-performance embedded systems due to its small size, low latency, and high throughput. It can be used as a stand-alone accelerator or integrated into a processor’s ALU or FPU.

articleTitle: Lifetime Analysis of Physically Damaged Electrolytic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Electrolytic capacitors, crucial in electronic circuits for charge storage, power regulation, and AC/DC conversion, rely on an oxide layer on the anode for their dielectric. Aluminum electrolytic capacitors are particularly valued for their high capacity and cost-effectiveness. However, they are sensitive to voltage, temperature changes, and reverse polarization, leading to various failure modes. As a result of these failure modes, they undergo catastrophic degradation. This paper will investigate the lifetime implications and usage risks of aluminum electrolytic capacitors used in production stages in the event of physical damage. The capacitance and ESR characteristics of aluminum electrolytic capabilities will be examined in order to determine the impact on lifetime. Special life tests will be performed on damaged components, and possible risks will be measured in a laboratory environment. This investigation aims to contribute to future research in this area. Furthermore, the possible failure modes and underlying causes of physically damaged components will be discussed.

articleTitle: An Agile Verification for Multi-core Processor Off-chip Memory System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Multi-core processors utilize off-chip DDR memory to provide high-bandwidth and large-capacity memory access. The off-chip memory system is crucial to processor chip research and development. Seventy percent of the research and development cycle is the verification time, because DDR memory design parameters and working modes are diverse, the verification is time-consuming and resource-consuming, and its verification often becomes the bottleneck of the entire research and development cycle. This paper presents an agile verification platform for off-chip memory systems for multi-core processors and introduces key technologies for improving the efficiency of agile verification. The proposed verification platform includes high-quality test programs and an optimized verification procedure. The test program uses directed and random tests based on prior knowledge and NSA (The Negative Selection Algorithm, NSA), respectively, and three acceleration strategies are designed for the initialization, debugging, and running phase of the verification procedure. To validate the effectiveness of the self-designed 16-core processor, the RTL code of an actual off-chip memory system is used as the verification object. The experimental results demonstrate that when the random test program case is reduced by 40%, there is a 29% improvement in the functional coverage and a 3 to 20 times improvement in verification efficiency. Additionally, a total of 26 design bugs are discovered across four categories. The verification results clearly indicate that the proposed method enhances verification efficiency and is ideal for full-chip functional test and regression test.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Logic Based Reconfigurable Digital CIM Macro for Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The imperative for energy efficiency in Artificial Intelligence (AI) aligns with global environmental sustainability goals, presenting substantial challenges. Compute-in-memory (CIM) offers a viable solution for edge computing, capitalizing on its superior energy efficiency and bandwidth. Yet, the specialized nature of CIM hardware impedes its broader adoption in AIoT applications. This study introduces a dynamically reconfigurable digital CIM leveraging dynamic logic to enhance energy efficiency. Dynamic logic reduces transistor count and transmission delay compared to static logic, thereby augmenting the energy efficiency ratio. It features a reconfigurable Manchester carry chain for adaptable computation across different data bit-widths and incorporates reusable computation units supporting seven operator types, minimizing circuit area. Evaluation using TSMC 40-nm CMOS technology demonstrates that the proposed macro circuit operates at 800 MHz at 1.1 V, achieving energy efficiencies of 0.76 TOPS/W for 8-bit multiplication and 4.22 TOPS/W for 8-bit addition at 0.8 V. Emulation of neural networks (NNs) within the AIoT framework demonstrates that a significant number of computational cycles can be executed using a minimal set of instructions.

articleTitle: An Extensible Legalization Framework for Multiple Physical Design Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Legalization tries to remove all overlaps with minimum wire-length or total displacement while meeting design rules as much as possible. In advanced technology circuit designs, many cells of multi-row height and complex design rules have brought challenges to legalization. Academic researches usually focus on the legalization problem of one particular design rule, and no legalization framework considers multiple design rules. Therefore, this paper presents an extensible and general legalization framework that can support the replacement of legalization algorithms and the expansion of design rules. First, we design a complete basic operation module compatible with multiple legalization algorithms. Then, we develop an extensible design rules checking module to satisfy numerous design rules and quickly support new rules. Finally, we propose two acceleration techniques for the framework. Experimental results show that our algorithm framework can achieve a 3% reduction on maximum cell displacement, a 7% reduction on average cell displacement, and 26% less legalization runtime than the state-of-the-art commercial tool Innovus when dealing with multiple design rules on test cases derived from industrial designs.

articleTitle: Securing Boundary Scan Chains: Encryption and Access Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: The Joint Test Action Group (JTAG) , an international standard testing protocol (IEEE 1149.1 compatible), is primarily used for internal chip testing to address chip testing issues. However, the powerful functionality of the JTAG poses a serious threat to the security of chips and devices when maliciously exploited. Due to the serial input nature of scan chain data, malicious users can use basic hardware to access data in the chain, leading to key or information leakage. They can also manipulate the test chain to cause abnormal data input/output or switch the circuit's operating mode, resulting in chip malfunction. To mitigate these threats, this paper designs and implements a hardware prototype system, including a stream encryption module and a Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) permission management module. The stream encryption module encrypts scan chain data to prevent unauthorized access, while the RBAC permission management module ensures that only authorized users or roles can access the corresponding scan chain data. By integrating these two modules and working in coordination with the JTAG, comprehensive protection of the scan chain is achieved. Experimental results demonstrate that the designed encryption monitoring scheme and permission allocation technology effectively protect the boundary scan chain from unauthorized access and malicious attacks. Furthermore, they can manage the usage permissions of authorized users to reduce the risk of unauthorized use in case of chip key leakage. Despite increased resource consumption in terms of time and space, the system remains within estimated ranges.

articleTitle: PreRoutSGAT: Pre-Routing Timing Prediction Based on Graph Neural Network with Global Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Circuits and Systems (ICCS)
abstract: Pre-routing Static Timing Analysis (STA) is pivotal in evaluating the timing functionality during digital design verification. Its accuracy and speed in assessing various node features within the circuit, including arrival time, slew, and slack, as well as edge features such as net delay and cell delay, have a profound impact on the entire digital design process. An unsatisfactory STA can lead to recurrent iterations of the entire placement and routing process, or even a redesign of RTL code. Leveraging the congruity between circuit timing paths and graph structures, we propose our Graph Neural Network (GNN) model, PreRoutSGAT (Pre-Routing Simple Global Attention), for prerouting timing prediction. We utilize a simple and effective residual structure to alleviate the prediction accuracy degradation brought by deep GNN, and greatly minimize the GPU memory usage required for training with a linear computational complexity attention convolution layer. Based on PreRoutSGAT, our approach encompasses three models that are built on the same concept, but differ slightly in structure. These disparate models are trained on 14 circuit timing graphs and evaluated on 7 graphs. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed models, in comparison to the previous SOTA model TimingGCN, achieve superior results in predicting multiple dimensions. Additionally, the proposed models achieve better performance and the average memory usage of the GPU is reduced by about 77.4% without increasing the time overhead.
